<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda Eatwell returns this summer to teach her much-loved yoga sessions, located on the stunning Lakeside Centre rooftop.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="684" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1024x684.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-26231" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1024x684.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-768x513.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1080x721.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-600x401.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-960x641.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08.jpg 1366w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Join us at the Lakeside Centre rooftop on Saturday mornings for a series of uplifting yoga sessions designed to help you start your weekend with intention, movement, and joy.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">What’s included in a session?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">You can expect a <strong>60-minute flow</strong> that is:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>Dynamic and energising</strong> – to wake up your body and clear your mind.</li>



<li><strong>Accessible to all levels</strong> – whether you’re new to yoga or have an established practice.</li>



<li><strong>Intention-led</strong> – helping you reconnect with yourself and the season.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Yoga mats are available on-site, but please feel free to bring your own if that is more comfortable. Please bring:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Comfortable clothes</li>



<li>A water bottle</li>
</ul>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Dates & Times</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Sessions will run on a Saturday morning:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>2nd May- 3rd October</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Start time: 10:00am. </strong>Please arrive 10-15 minutes before the start of the session. Late entry <strong>may not </strong>be possible due to the layout of the building.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Please note, there are no classes on August 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd</em>,<em> and September 12th.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Book your session now on Eventbrite.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access Information</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The nearest public transport station is Abbey Wood (National Rail, Elizabeth Line).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">You can access the Lakeside Centre by bus routes 177, 244, 229, 301, 401, 472.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note parking is available but limited.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bike shed on site.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Lakeside Centre facilities: Public toilets with wheelchair access and baby changing facilities.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For full access information and queries, please email pandp@bowarts.com.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Amanda Eatwell</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Outside of yoga, Amanda is a fine art and documentary photographer, based in Thamesmead. She has had two solo exhibitions at The Lakeside Centre, and has played an active role in the Thamesmead Festival for the past three years – creating an art installation one year, and helping with production in 2025. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda has practiced yoga since her twenties, and qualified as a BoxingYoga coach nine years ago. This is where the dynamic yoga class stems from: a unique yoga-based training system that was originally born to help boxers reach new levels of performance through improved core strength, body awareness, balance and flexibility. Amanda provides a friendly and inclusive environment for her classes. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda is a keen runner, with several marathons under her belt. She can confirm that stretching and strengthening through yoga support her physically and mentally through every aspect of her life! You can find out more about Amanda’s Yoga sessions on her Instagram account <a href="https://www.instagram.com/amandaeatwelldoesyoga?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==" type="link" id="https://www.instagram.com/amandaeatwelldoesyoga?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==">@amandaeatwelldoesyoga</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Lakeside Centre</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Looking for things to do at the Lakeside Centre?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Grab a cup of coffee or a bite to eat at the Thamesmead Social cafe, overlooking the Southmere Lake.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Visit the <a href="https://www.lakesidedarkroom.com/">Lakeside Darkroom</a> and learn about analogue photography with workshops on how to use use an analogue camera, process film, & more!</p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">RCRDSHOP Live Lounge at Oaklands Social</h1>		
<div id="post-29557" class="post-29557 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-live-talks location-oaklands-rise cat_live-talks">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Saturday 29th August 2026					 
, 7:30pm to 10:30pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h5 class="wp-block-heading" style="font-size:20px">Join London’s finest soul and hip hop music collective, RCRDSHOP, as they once again take over Oaklands Social. Enjoy an evening of London’s best emerging artists playing alongside the RCRDSHOP live band. </h5>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Picture1.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29558"/><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">RCRDSHOP at Oaklands Social</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">RCRDSHOP Live Lounge returns to Oaklands Social for an intimate night of live soul, hip hop and good energy, bringing together some of London’s most exciting emerging artists with the unmistakable sound of the RCRDSHOP live band. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Known for championing under-the-radar talent and creating carefully curated live music experiences, RCRDSHOP has become a home for artists and audiences who love discovering new sounds. Welcoming audiences back for our tenth collaboration with RCRDSHOP, Oaklands Social invites you into a community-focused setting where standout vocalists, rappers and musicians share the stage, reworking original tracks and soulful favourites with live-band arrangements. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Expect an evening filled with rich vocals, sharp lyricism, groove-led instrumentation and the kind of atmosphere that only comes from live music in an intimate venue. Come through, bring your friends, and settle in for a night of live performances, drinks and feel-good energy at Oaklands Social. </p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Bow Families: creating your own puppet deities with Nicola McEvoy</h1>		
<div id="post-28100" class="post-28100 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tag-bow-families tribe_events_cat-family-friendly-event location-bow-road cat_family-friendly-event">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Sunday 30th August 2026					 
, 11:00am to 1:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Join artist Nicola McEvoy to make different mythological creatures or deities and work collectively to make a shared ‘chimera’ – a monster composed of many animals. Open to children and families of all ages – all materials provided.</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="767" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-1024x767.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-28072" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-1024x767.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-300x225.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-768x576.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-1536x1151.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-1080x809.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-640x480.jpg 640w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-600x450.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-560x420.jpg 560w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities-960x720.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Puppet-Dieities.jpg 1920w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image credit: Nicola McEvoy</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Don’t miss the final day of the Bow Open exhibition, and a chance to take part in our family workshop as we make different mythological creatures or deities and work collectively to make a shared ‘chimera’ – a monster composed of many animals. Open to children and families of all ages – all materials provided.   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In this workshop, children will learn new skills in paper folding and collage with creativity, as well as engage in a highly collaborative making session. Nicola will make printouts/templates for different mythological creatures/deities. <br> <br><em>This event is an inclusive, friendly environment which is accessible to all abilities and age groups.   </em>  <br> <br><em>Bow Families is a series of free, drop-in family art workshops that take place on the last Sunday of every month in the Bow Arts Courtyard. These sessions are a wonderful opportunity for local families to get creative and try something new! Each session is led by a Bow Arts’ Artist and all materials are provided.</em> <br> </p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>More about Nicola McEvoy</strong> <br> <br>Nicola McEvoy is a transdisciplinary artist who works across the mediums of analogue/digital video, cameraless photography, textiles and ceramics. Her practice-based research, ‘Television Alchemy’, investigates the liquid materiality of CRT TV. She explores the correspondences between moving image and dream as it emerges from the primordial waters of chaos. Nicola is a graduate of the Royal College of Art and Goldsmiths, University of London. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">As an artist educator and facilitator, she has worked with children and young people, as well as adults with learning disabilities. <br> <br><strong>Access information </strong>   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Bow Arts Trust courtyard room has step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system.  Accessible parking is not available on-site but blue badge parking can be found 500m away on Fairfield Road.    </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)    </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a table near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Transport Information   </strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Opening hours: Mon-Friday, 9am to 5pm    <br>Address: Bow Arts Trust, 183 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ    <br>Nearest station(s): Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away.    <br>Bus: 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area.    <br>Bike: Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station. </p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Knitting the Air: The Exhibition</h1>		
<div id="post-26760" class="post-26760 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-guest-exhibition location-bow-road cat_guest-exhibition">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
				Friday 4th September 2026 – Sunday  20th September 2026			 
, 10:00am to 4:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-medium-font-size">Knitting the Air presents a free exhibition exploring air pollution, place, and community made by 132 knitters from across Poplar, Bow and wider east London.</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-1024x683.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-26815" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-1024x683.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-768x512.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-1536x1024.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-2048x1365.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-1080x720.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-1920x1280.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-600x400.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Knitting-Landscape_Credit_Rakib_Syed-960x640.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">The Big Reveal showcase of the completed data, September 2025, Photo: Rakib Syed</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">What does the air you breathe look like? For 132 knitters from Poplar, Bow and east London, the answer took shape over two and a half years, stitch by stitch, as a 13-metre knitted textile that translates a year of air pollution data into something you can both see and touch.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">At the heart of this exhibition is the knitting itself: a vivid, large-scale work created from readings gathered by two Breathe London Communities sensors located in Poplar, one near the A12 and one at the Blackwall Tunnel approach. It visualised two pollutants which are harmful for our health, Nitrogen Dioxide and Particulate Matter 2.5. Alongside it, objects and materials from the making process reveal the skill, care and collective effort behind every knitted row, tracing the journey from raw scientific data to something handmade, tactile and human.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="724" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-1024x724.png" alt="" class="wp-image-26768" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-1024x724.png 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-300x212.png 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-768x543.png 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-1080x764.png 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-600x425.png 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small-960x679.png 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A12-Particulate-Matter-2.5-September-2023_small.png 1200w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Knitted data from the A12 sensor, Particulate Matter 2.5, September 2023, September 2023</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This exhibition is also about voices. A new film shines a spotlight on the knitters themselves, the residents who gave thousands of hours of their time to make this work, sharing what it meant to knit data about the air in their own neighbourhood, and what that process revealed about the place they call home. Their reflections sit alongside more than 400 responses gathered from the wider community, capturing what air quality means to people across east London. Their reflections bring everyday experiences of air pollution into focus, highlighting their concerns for their health, hopes for change and a deep appreciation that clean air is fundamental to life.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-gallery has-nested-images columns-default is-cropped wp-block-gallery-1 is-layout-flex wp-block-gallery-is-layout-flex">

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A public programme of free creative workshops, events and talks accompanies the exhibition, inviting people to explore air, place and community, to connect with the work and share their perspectives.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Together, the textile, the objects, the film, and the community voices make the invisible visible. Modern air pollution can be easy to overlook when it cannot be seen. Here, it becomes a shared story and a living archive, told through wool and data, by hands and hours, and in the words of the people who live with it every day.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Knitting the Air: The Exhibition is supported using public funding from <strong>Arts Council England </strong>and in partnership with <strong>The Aberfeldy Practice, Imperial College London, Bow Arts Trust</strong> and <strong>London College of Fashion</strong>.</em></p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>More about Knitting the Air / Caroline Murray</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Knitting the Air is a collective community art project blending science, data, art and community, using knitting to visualise air pollution data in Poplar, east London. Largely invisible and intangible to most, air pollution is one of the most pressing environmental risks to public health in the UK. Knitting the Air aims to make that scientific data accessible, tangible and personal.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Through the combined efforts of 132 knitters across Poplar, Bow and east London, the project has produced a 13-metre textile translating a year of air quality data into something handmade and human, inviting people to connect with the data that shapes their daily lives and to share their own stories about the air they breathe.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Knitting the Air is led by Caroline Murray, a creative community practitioner and textile artist. Working across knitting, quilting and weaving, her practice explores how collective making can foster connection, meaning and care – for ourselves, for one another and with the world around us.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://www.instagram.com/knittingtheair/" type="link" id="https://www.instagram.com/knittingtheair/">@knittingtheair</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access information</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Nunnery Gallery and Cafe have step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Accessible parking is not available on-site but blue badge parking can be found 500m away on Fairfield Road.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a table near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Opening hours: </strong>Tues-Sun, 10am to 4pm</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Address:</strong> Nunnery Gallery, 181 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Nearest station(s):</strong> Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bus:</strong> 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bike:</strong> Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda Eatwell returns this summer to teach her much-loved yoga sessions, located on the stunning Lakeside Centre rooftop.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="684" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1024x684.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-26231" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1024x684.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-768x513.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-1080x721.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-600x401.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08-960x641.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/y-08.jpg 1366w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Join us at the Lakeside Centre rooftop on Saturday mornings for a series of uplifting yoga sessions designed to help you start your weekend with intention, movement, and joy.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">What’s included in a session?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">You can expect a <strong>60-minute flow</strong> that is:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>Dynamic and energising</strong> – to wake up your body and clear your mind.</li>



<li><strong>Accessible to all levels</strong> – whether you’re new to yoga or have an established practice.</li>



<li><strong>Intention-led</strong> – helping you reconnect with yourself and the season.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Yoga mats are available on-site, but please feel free to bring your own if that is more comfortable. Please bring:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Comfortable clothes</li>



<li>A water bottle</li>
</ul>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Dates & Times</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Sessions will run on a Saturday morning:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>2nd May- 3rd October</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Start time: 10:00am. </strong>Please arrive 10-15 minutes before the start of the session. Late entry <strong>may not </strong>be possible due to the layout of the building.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Please note, there are no classes on August 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd</em>,<em> and September 12th.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Book your session now on Eventbrite.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access Information</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The nearest public transport station is Abbey Wood (National Rail, Elizabeth Line).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">You can access the Lakeside Centre by bus routes 177, 244, 229, 301, 401, 472.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note parking is available but limited.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bike shed on site.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Lakeside Centre facilities: Public toilets with wheelchair access and baby changing facilities.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For full access information and queries, please email pandp@bowarts.com.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Amanda Eatwell</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Outside of yoga, Amanda is a fine art and documentary photographer, based in Thamesmead. She has had two solo exhibitions at The Lakeside Centre, and has played an active role in the Thamesmead Festival for the past three years – creating an art installation one year, and helping with production in 2025. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda has practiced yoga since her twenties, and qualified as a BoxingYoga coach nine years ago. This is where the dynamic yoga class stems from: a unique yoga-based training system that was originally born to help boxers reach new levels of performance through improved core strength, body awareness, balance and flexibility. Amanda provides a friendly and inclusive environment for her classes. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Amanda is a keen runner, with several marathons under her belt. She can confirm that stretching and strengthening through yoga support her physically and mentally through every aspect of her life! You can find out more about Amanda’s Yoga sessions on her Instagram account <a href="https://www.instagram.com/amandaeatwelldoesyoga?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==" type="link" id="https://www.instagram.com/amandaeatwelldoesyoga?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==">@amandaeatwelldoesyoga</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Lakeside Centre</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Looking for things to do at the Lakeside Centre?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Grab a cup of coffee or a bite to eat at the Thamesmead Social cafe, overlooking the Southmere Lake.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Visit the <a href="https://www.lakesidedarkroom.com/">Lakeside Darkroom</a> and learn about analogue photography with workshops on how to use use an analogue camera, process film, & more!</p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Bow Skills workshop: re-imagining city landscapes with poetry and wandering with Jazzy Green</h1>		
<div id="post-28316" class="post-28316 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-events-for-artists-and-creatives tribe_events_cat-workshop location-bow-road cat_events-for-artists-and-creatives cat_workshop">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Saturday 5th September 2026					 
, 11:00am to 1:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Every day we walk our urban city scape with stories and poetry flying past us, unnoticed. How does our culture of productivity and routine thieve our ability to notice and re-imagine everyday ephemera around us? Join poet Jazzy Green for an accessible writing workshop open to anyone with an interest in poetry and movement as creative practice.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="768" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-1024x768.jpeg" alt="" class="wp-image-28317" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-1024x768.jpeg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-300x225.jpeg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-768x576.jpeg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-1536x1152.jpeg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-2048x1536.jpeg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-1080x810.jpeg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-1920x1440.jpeg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-640x480.jpeg 640w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-600x450.jpeg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-560x420.jpeg 560w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-credit-Jazzy-Green-960x720.jpeg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image: Jazzy Green</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">To begin, we will meet in the Bow Arts Courtyard then walk to the park behind to do an icebreaker/ movement game to get out of our heads and into our bodies. Jazzy will then lead the group along a pre-planned route, meandering through residential areas, by the canal and through green space to end up in Victoria Park.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Maps and route-making force us to move in determined paths and directions, so this workshop will challenge us to stay present and be led by observations that draw us in along the way. During the walk, we will utilise elements of Dérive, a wandering practice developed by French philosopher Guy Debord and techniques Jazzy uses in their own practice such as Emotional Memory Mapping – the act of marking your emotional state and observations in relation to space.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Each participant will be provided with a printed map encompassing the areas we will wander, along with a pen.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Once we reach Victoria Park, we will have some lunch and share our experiences and observations before crafting a poem using the material gathered. We will look at the importance of specificity in a poem, and how to write orbitally around a central feeling or topic with the images collected from the urban landscape.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">There will be an opportunity to share your creations and discussion of how they can transform into more evolved pieces. We welcome all kinds of artists as exercises of observation and imagination can be translated into any artistic discipline beyond the written word.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">All we ask you to bring is your own notepad, small enough to carry whilst walking. Maps, pens and snacks will be provided. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In this workshop, you will:  </p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Learn a technique of urban wandering that encourages presence and observation of our surroundings </li>
</ul>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Know how to use Emotional Memory Mapping to track how place (architecture, objects, movement) makes us feel and behave </li>
</ul>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Develop an understanding of how navigating space in relation to emotion rather than commercial function develops a surreal, poetic way of writing about place, and the importance of this as capital projects rapidly uproot communities </li>
</ul>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Understand how to use poetic techniques such as Cut Out, Freewriting, Collage Poetry and Orbital Writing to produce unique and specific imagery in response to place </li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This workshop is open to anyone to attend but will particularly resonate with artists who have a profound interest in poetry writing. No previous experience is required – come along and find out! </p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>More about Jazzy Green</strong> <br>Jazzy Green is a poet, performer, lover of natural landscapes and everyday groover. You can find their debut poetry collection ‘Did You See My Eyes Mum’ (2024) from New Words Press. They have performed / produced work for Mad Jack’s Theatre, Roundhouse, Boy Blue’s Project Revolution, Moi Ko collective, at the New York City Poetry Festival, for Queer Poetics Research Collective and at various poetry nights across London and NYC. Their writing and performance focus on grief, attachment, queer love and tangibility. They were part of the Roundhouse Poetry Collective 25-26, and Anthony Anaxagorou’s advanced poetry workshop ‘Close Read’ with Poetry School. They believe real accolades are in our everyday interactions with friends, strangers, and the landscapes we embed in.  <br> <br> <br><strong>About Bow Skills  </strong> <br> <br>Bow Arts seeks to support creative professionals at all stages of their careers. In 2015, Bow Arts launched <a href="https://bowarts.org/artist-opportunities/bow-skills" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bow Skills</a> in response to an artist survey which showed over 90% of practicing artists find it useful to receive further support outside formal education.   <br> <br>Bow Skills is a dynamic and relevant programme of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) which is informed by an artist steering group and open to all creative practitioners across London. The programme of talks, panel discussions, new skills labs and peer crits is open to all, with concession rates available to students, over 65s, under 18s, Bow Arts artists and key workers.  <br> <br>Access information    <br> <br>The Bow Arts Trust courtyard have step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system. Accessible parking is not available on-site.  <br> <br>If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)    <br> <br>Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a seat near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!  <br> <br><strong>Transport Information    </strong><br> <br>Opening hours: Mon-Fri, 9am-5pm <br>Address: Bow Arts Trust, 183 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ    <br>Nearest station(s): Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away.    <br>Bus: 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area.    <br>Bike: Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station. </p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Thamesmead Wildlife Wanders: Autumn Walk with J D Swann</h1>		
<div id="post-29340" class="post-29340 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-workshop location-lakeside-centre cat_workshop">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Saturday 12th September 2026					 
, 11:00am to 1:30pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h5 class="wp-block-heading" style="font-size:20px"><em>A seasonal wildlife walk in Thamesmead with ornithological investigator J D Swann, with an emphasis on observation of birds, local ecology and history.</em></h5>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="768" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-1024x768.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29342" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-1024x768.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-300x225.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-768x576.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-1080x810.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-640x480.jpg 640w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-600x450.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-560x420.jpg 560w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML-960x720.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/05WildlifeWanderJD0626SML.jpg 1500w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image credit: J D Swann</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A seasonal wildlife walk in Thamesmead with ornithological investigator J D Swann, with emphasis on observation of birds, local ecology and history.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The walk will start by Southmere Lake outside Thamesmead Social café. The walk will loop around Birchmere Lake, Hawksmoor Park, and Butts Woods, past TUMP 53, and follow the canals of Thamesmead ending back at the cafe. WC’s and refreshments can be found at Thamesmead Social Café.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">J D encourages participants to bring binoculars and cameras for documentation, and at the end there will be a review of what has been seen.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">There will be J D Swann stamped notebooks available free for people who wish to document observations. If you have attended before, please bring your notebook.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This event is the third of three seasonal walks with J D Swann.</p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Community Outdoor Cinema: Disney’s Encanto at Royal Albert Wharf</h1>		
<div id="post-29702" class="post-29702 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-family-friendly-event tribe_events_cat-film-screening location-royal-albert-wharf cat_family-friendly-event cat_film-screening">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Saturday 12th September 2026					 
, 7:00pm to 10:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-large-font-size">Join us on the dock for a free outdoor cinema screening of Disney’s Encanto! Grab a pair of our cinema headphones, settle into a deck chair, grab some popcorn, and enjoy a magical evening by the water with family, friends, and neighbours of all ages as we celebrate the end of summer together at Royal Albert Wharf.</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29703" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061-768x512.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061-600x400.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/RoyalAlbertWharfOpenStudios_2026©BethanyParkinson_061-960x640.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image: Bethany Parkinson</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Celebrate the end of summer with a feel-good outdoor cinema night at Royal Albert Wharf. Join us on the Royal Albert Wharf dock for a free screening of Disney’s Encanto, a colourful, music-filled family favourite for all ages. Bring the family, meet up with friends, or come along with neighbours and settle in for a relaxed evening in Pump House Square. This is a welcoming night out for children, families, and of course grown-ups too!</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Deck chairs will be available, with bags of popcorn on offer to purchase to complete the cinema experience and a paid bar open for drinks throughout the evening. A limited number of deckchairs will be available to use; however, we encourage attendees to bring their own chairs/blankets and cushions to sit on to avoid disappointment.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Entry is free, but capacity is limited, so arrive early, get comfy, and enjoy a magical summer evening under the open sky. Please check timings below.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>More about the film</strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Walt Disney Animation Studios’ <em>Encanto</em> follows the Madrigals, an extraordinary family living in a magical house in the mountains of Colombia. Every child is blessed with a unique gift except Mirabel. When she finds the family’s magic is in danger, she learns she may be their last hope. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This film is rated <strong>PG</strong> by the MPAA for some thematic elements and mild peril. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access information</strong> <br>This is an outdoor, ground-floor event with accessible viewing spaces available near the cinema area, including a limited number of wheelchair-accessible spaces. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Accessible toilets are available on site, a short walk from the cinema area. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions about accessibility at this event, or if you would like to let us know about any access requirements in advance of attending, please email <a href="mailto:pandp@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">pandp@bowarts.com</a> and we’ll be happy to help. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Transport information</strong><strong>    </strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Pump House Square, Royal Albert Wharf, London, E16 2QP. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">What3Word: ///port.boxing.movie </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Nearest station(s): Gallions Reach (DLR) </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bus: 129, 262, 474, 366, SL2 </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Parking: No parking available </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bike: Limited lockable rings bike parking available </p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Bow Skills workshop: bid writing and arts fundraising with Kim Pearce – an Arts Council England special! </h1>		
<div id="post-28321" class="post-28321 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-events-for-artists-and-creatives tribe_events_cat-workshop location-bow-road cat_events-for-artists-and-creatives cat_workshop">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Wednesday 16th September 2026					 
, 6:00pm to 8:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-medium-font-size">Join experienced arts fundraiser <strong>Kim Pearce </strong>in this Arts Council England (ACE) project grants special, as she demystifies the four investment principles, breaks down the application structure, and provides practical insights into how to build out a successful ACE bid.  The workshop will end with a Q&A where you can put your burning questions to Kim about specific ideas or issues you’re coming up against! </h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large is-resized"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="797" height="1024" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-797x1024.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-28322" style="aspect-ratio:0.7783288064210944;width:840px;height:auto" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-797x1024.jpg 797w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-233x300.jpg 233w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-768x987.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-1195x1536.jpg 1195w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-1594x2048.jpg 1594w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-840x1080.jpg 840w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-1494x1920.jpg 1494w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-600x771.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic-747x960.jpg 747w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Kim-Directing-pic.jpg 1960w" sizes="(max-width: 797px) 100vw, 797px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">After a broad overview of the different types of funding out there for artists, Kim will take a deep dive into the specifics of ACE project grants and DYCP</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In an artist-centred approach, she will demystify the ACE investment principles and talk through how to deploy her grant writing technique as a tactile, practical blueprint to engage with these principles.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Kim will then deconstruct what goes behind an ACE bid – pulling apart the application structure, drilling down into how to build out responses to individual questions, and running through example answers to tease out useful tips and tricks that you can apply to your own bids.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The workshop will end with a Q&A, where you can put your burning questions to Kim and dive into specific questions you have about ACE project grants you’re working on or arts fundraising in general.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">All participants will get to take home a resource pack at the end, featuring everything you’ll have learnt in the session and some extra insights.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In this workshop, you will:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>Gain insights to develop ideas and write grant applications to support your practice</li>



<li>Learn how to bring a project idea to life and support the grant writing process</li>



<li>Master the updated guidelines of ACE project grants and DYCP to build out a successful bid</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This event will take place at Courtyard Room, Bow Arts Trust, 183 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Kim Pearce</strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Kim Pearce is a theatre director and producer with a decade of ACE funded projects to her name. Between 2016-2024, she was co-Artistic Director of Papergang Theatre, successfully running the company on a project by project basis. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Bow Skills </strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bow Arts seeks to support creative professionals at all stages of their careers. In 2015 Bow Arts launched <a href="https://bowarts.org/artist-opportunities/bow-skills" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bow Skills</a> in response to an artist survey which showed over 90% of practicing artists find it useful to receive further support outside formal education.   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bow Skills is a dynamic and relevant programme of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) which is informed by an artist steering group and open to all creative practitioners across London. The programme of talks, panel discussions, new skills labs and peer crits is open to all, with concession rates available to students, over 65s, under 18s, Bow Arts artists and key workers.   </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access information    <br></strong> <br>The Bow Arts Trust offices have step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system. Accessible parking is not available on-site.  <br> <br>If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)    <br> <br>Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a seat near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!  <br> <br><strong>Transport Information </strong>   <br> <br>Opening hours: Mon-Fri, 9am-5pm <br>Address: Bow Arts Trust, 183 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ    <br>Nearest station(s): Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away.    <br>Bus: 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area.    <br>Bike: Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station. <br> </p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Lakeside Centre Performance Evening</h1>		
<div id="post-29333" class="post-29333 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tribe_events_cat-live-talks location-lakeside-centre cat_live-talks">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
					Friday 18th September 2026					 
, 6:00pm to 9:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h5 class="wp-block-heading" style="font-size:20px"><em><em>Join us at the Lakeside Centre for a dynamic and collaborative evening of performance. Led by artist Joanna Penso, and featuring work</em></em> <em>by multidisciplinary artist Gusty Ferro<em>, explore performance through an undiscovered lens.</em></em></h5>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="576" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-1024x576.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29387" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-1024x576.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-300x169.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-768x432.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-1536x864.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-2048x1152.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-1080x607.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-1920x1080.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-600x337.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/JP-ALB-960x540.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image credit: Alberto Romano</figcaption></figure>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size"><strong>To Be Rendered</strong></h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>To Be Rendered</em> is a collaborative piece performed by artist Joanna Penso and glitch musician Alessandro La Barbera.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Sounds of the body in movement are amplified using stethoscope microphones, presenting intimate body noises as art material.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">From the mixing desk, La Barbera assumes control over the sounds produced by Penso’s movements, progressively warping and processing them until they bear little resemblance to their original source. Through the use of loopers, he layers these transformed sounds into pulsating rhythmic patterns.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Expansive breaths trigger recordings collected underwater in the Mediterranean Sea, resting heart beats transform into sounds from outer space. The female performer is treated as a vessel for a voice that is not her own.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Observed both visually and acoustically with microphones strapped to her body, Penso’s performance fluctuates between concious and unconcious movement.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Exploring power dynamics between the male and female, the performers tussle for control over the audio output, raising the question ‘whose voice gets to be heard?’</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size"><strong>TRANSMEAD listening event and live act by Gusty Ferro</strong></h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-resized"><img decoding="async" width="739" height="739" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-30087" style="width:671px;height:auto" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop.jpg 739w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-300x300.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-150x150.jpg 150w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-600x600.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-560x560.jpg 560w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-75x75.jpg 75w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-180x180.jpg 180w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/gusty_1983_crop-360x360.jpg 360w" sizes="(max-width: 739px) 100vw, 739px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Image credit: Gusty Ferro</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Multidisciplinary artist Gusty Ferro brings a deeply exploratory approach to sound through <a href="https://gbr01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mixcloud.com%2FRTM_FM%2Ftransmead-gusty-ferro-09072026%2F&data=05%7C02%7Camaltby%40bowarts.com%7Cfceef73929574219b89808def71b95fe%7Cbcde9fa1a41e4b04ab5f15633c8541cb%7C0%7C0%7C639219895113163940%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=csUka%2BICJ0NdfVqc7KIsCgzq5p2poUuZM472B6wUKy0%3D&reserved=0">TRANSMEAD</a>, a monthly programme at <a href="https://gbr01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Frtm.fm%2F&data=05%7C02%7Camaltby%40bowarts.com%7Cfceef73929574219b89808def71b95fe%7Cbcde9fa1a41e4b04ab5f15633c8541cb%7C0%7C0%7C639219895113198995%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=hl%2BfDXZ%2FMVYk%2FqsCaXEGStnGp6CxZ5lQ%2F%2F7XzzUbzzY%3D&reserved=0">RTM.FM</a> that presents a carefully curated selection of experimental and genre-defying music from artists working today.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Each episode combines newly discovered sonic experiments with selections from Gusty’s extensive personal archive of vinyl records, cassette tapes and digital collections. The result is a constantly evolving journey through contemporary underground music, where unexpected textures and bold artistic voices coexist. TRANSMEAD embodies a spirit of discovery, offering listeners a window into adventurous sounds that challenge traditional genre boundaries.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size"><strong>TRANSMEAD Live</strong> Act</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Gusty Ferro is improvising live with modular synthesisers, sampling field recordings- including material from their recent residency in Latvia; and using contact mic to generate a shapeshifting noise soundscape. Creating abstract narratives through sound, Gusty revisits memories of lived experiences and invites listeners to inhabit a fictional space where identities transform and perceptions merge into a new place.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Gusty says (in quote from text produced for the exhibition WITHIN at Dom Gallery, in Riga, July 2026):</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“I have been thinking about this fictional place called TRANSMEAD, that is also the name of my radio programme on experimental music at <a href="https://gbr01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Frtm.fm%2F&data=05%7C02%7Camaltby%40bowarts.com%7Cfceef73929574219b89808def71b95fe%7Cbcde9fa1a41e4b04ab5f15633c8541cb%7C0%7C0%7C639219895113220196%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=erte9z6o1S589FSTxnysd%2Bd8asjy%2FVO0sBAI2ckiHv0%3D&reserved=0">rtm.fm</a>. I live in an estate in South East London that is going through a phase of redevelopment and partial demolition. The whole environment surrounding where I stay has been shaping my lived experience in the city and one of the materials that I am interested in this context is the perforated metal used to ‘cage’ empty properties. I started to experiment with this metal mesh in relation to light and the shift in perception that happens depending on the spatial conditions created. It also changes the behaviour of sound in space and the contact microphones attached to it captures resonance and generates feedback loops – that is something I explore in my live performances where I improvise with modular synthesisers, sampling field recordings, patching modulations and delay effects to create temporal distortions and granular synthesis.”</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Joanna Penso</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Joanna Penso is a Yorkshire artist based in London. Her work centres sounds of the body and gut listening as a vehicle to understanding oneself, one another and the environment around us. Her research paper: <em>The Body as Site</em> was delivered at the Centre for Research into Sound Art Practice in 2024 and forms the basis of her on-going practice-based research. In 2024 she was awarded a DYCP grant to expand her practice into live performance. From this experimentation and upskilling period evolved a solo live performance using body amplification; <em>Body Talks</em>, which was shown at Divfuse Projects and The Nunnery Gallery, 2025. Her crowd-funded film <em>Digestion Symphony</em>, depicting performative eating to the beat of an ever-quickening metronome was shown at Aesthetica Art Prize in 2023. Penso currently has a regular radio programme on <a href="https://gbr01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fresonance.fm%2F&data=05%7C02%7Cjcase%40bowarts.com%7C65a6ea475edb4626586908deec79dc0d%7Cbcde9fa1a41e4b04ab5f15633c8541cb%7C0%7C0%7C639208207281385899%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=hkCIw1eRIIrjI028xzjdp%2BPbieT2%2Fl6tjs3u%2FPZqRcQ%3D&reserved=0" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Resonance.FM</a>:  <em>Come Digest With Me</em>, featuring international artists, curators, chefs, historians and doctors. She has delivered workshops for Dorich House Museum and has exhibited at Pushkin House, York Art Gallery, APT Gallery, Southwark Park Galleries and at St Ives September Fest.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Alessandro La Barbera</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Alessandro La Barbera is a musician and producer from Palermo, Sicily, adopted by London in 2010. His work blends triphop, electro-acoustic beats, glitch music and sampling. He is a founder of artist collective HolyShift; a regular music event in London and Berlin giving artists the chance to try out new music in front of live audiences. La Barbera has been teaching music and music production in schools and charities for over a decade, also delivering workshops for neurodivergent people at the award-winning charity Lewisham Music. He works independently in music production and mixing engineering at Studio 18 in South Bermondsey having contributed towards the work of Sans Sousis, Davide Shorty, TJoe Cheung, Natalie Oliveri, Maria Chiara Argiro, Apathy Khea and Jamie Leeming.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Transport Information </strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Tube Station</strong>: Abbey Wood (National Rail, Elizabeth Line). <br><strong>Bus</strong>: 117, 229, 401, 472, 601, 301, 602, 669, N1 <br>Please note parking is not available. There is a bike shed on site. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access Information</strong> </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Lakeside Centre has step-free access throughout from street level, with access via the lifts to upper floor studios and the exhibition space. Accessible toilets are available on the ground floor and first floor, with baby change facilities available via Thamesmead Social cafe. This venue does not have a hearing loop system. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For full access information and queries, please email pandp@bowarts.com. </p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-large-font-size"><strong>Opening Times</strong></h2>



<p class="has-lgrey-background-color has-background has-wpdc-medium-font-size wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Private View:</strong> Friday 18th September, 6-9pm<br><strong>Lakeside Centre Open Art Studios:</strong> Saturday 19th September, 12-6pm<br><strong>By appointment only:</strong> Thursday 24th September, Friday 25th September, Saturday 26th September, Thursday 1st October, Friday 2nd October, Saturday 3rd October. Between 12-6pm.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">About the exhibition</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>On the Wall</em> explores how physical movement through the landscape shapes artistic process, offering audiences an intimate perspective on Britain’s and Spain’s climbing environments and the communities that inhabit them.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A collaborative exhibition bringing together painter Alexander Heaton and photographer Jonathan Blower. Their work explores climbing as more than a subject – it is a way of seeing.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Heaton produces paintings inspired by exhibitions to mountains and crags, translating sketches, memories, and direct observation into expressive landscapes that evoke the physical and emotional experience of being immersed in challenging terrain. His work captures the shifting light, texture, and atmosphere encountered on the rock face, where moments of stillness exist alongside exertion and exposure.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Blower’s photographic practice documents climbers within these same environments. Rather than focusing on achievements or spectacle, his photographs reveal the relationship between people, place and movement. Made on crags throughout the UK and Spain, the images record fleeting moments of concentration, trust, and vulnerability, celebrating climbing as a shared culture built on cooperation, respect, and connection with the natural landscape.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Through an interplay of painting and photography, the exhibition invites visitors to rethink how we experience the natural world and how artistic practice can emerge from direct physical engagement with it.</p>

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Bhajan Hunjan: speaking through materials</h1>		
<div id="post-26297" class="post-26297 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tag-exhibition tag-nunnery-gallery tribe_events_cat-exhibitions location-bow-road cat_exhibitions">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
				Friday 9th October 2026 – Sunday  20th December 2026			 
, 10:00am to 4:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" style="font-size:20px">We’re delighted to present a solo exhibition from artist and long-time studio holder Bhajan Hunjan. <em>Bhajan Hunjan: speaking through materials</em> will, for the first time, bring together works from Hunjan’s rich and various career to date, spanning over 40 years of practice.</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image alignwide size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2500" height="1876" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-26298" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989.jpg 2500w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-300x225.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-1024x768.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-768x576.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-1536x1153.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-2048x1537.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-1080x810.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-1920x1441.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-640x480.jpg 640w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-600x450.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-560x420.jpg 560w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Painting-She-Observed-Acrylic-on-canvas-3-x-5-ft-1989-960x720.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 2500px) 100vw, 2500px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Bhajan Hunjan, <em>She observed</em>, acrylic on canvas, 1989</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hunjan’s ambitious and dextrous use of materials has tied together her practice both in and outside of the gallery. The exhibition will take us on a journey to explore this dexterity, bringing together print, painting, sculpture and collage from across Hunjan’s career. The show will also bring to light Hunjan’s innovation with materials within public art – such as silk-screen printed glass, laser-cut acrylic and metal, and stonework – together with documentation of the closely collaborative working process behind her public artworks. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Guided by a unique visual language of line, rhythmic pattern and symbols, Hunjan’s work pushes the boundaries of meaning as well as materials, often speaking powerfully for women and diaspora communities. Drawing on her Kenyan upbringing, Sikh heritage and experience of moving to the UK in the 1970s, Hunjan’s work plays an important role in the history of women artists. She participated in the Black British Art Movement, exhibiting and curating alongside contemporaries, and has been included in numerous exhibitions and publications exploring the movement since, most recently in Tate Britain’s 2023 touring exhibition <em>Women In Revolt! Art and Activism in the UK 1970-1990</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">An accompanying publication, supported by the Paul Mellon Centre, will illustrate all exhibition works, for the first time celebrating Hunjan’s extensive work collectively in print. Newly commissioned essays will tell the stories behind her works, as well as commenting on the important contribution she has made to British art. A public programme will also accompany the exhibition, providing opportunities for all ages to further engage with Hunjan’s work.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>About Bhajan Hunjan</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Born in Kenya, Bhajan Hunjan moved to the UK in the mid-1970s to study at Reading University and the Slade. From the 1980s onwards she exhibited at spaces including the Indian Artists (UK) Gallery, Aspex Gallery, Brixton Art Gallery, Horizon Gallery and through the collective she co-founded, Panchayat. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hunjan’s work forms part of a wider search for visibility among South Asian and Black women artists in 1980s and 1990s Britain. Her experiences working at a South Asian women’s refuge in Reading deepened her focus on women’s interior lives and the dignity of representation. “<em>My work at present is about my experiences, women, and in particular Asian women</em>”, she stated in 1986. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">From the 1990s onwards, Hunjan turned increasingly toward public commissions – murals and large-scale floor works developed in collaboration with women’s and community groups, such as floorscapes in Leicester town centre and The Town Square, Slough, and the St. Paul’s Way Transformation project with Bow Arts in Tower Hamlets, London. Alongside, Hunjan worked extensively as an artist-educator across east London.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hunjan’s contribution to feminist and diasporic art histories has gained renewed recognition through ‘Women in Revolt! Art and Activism in the UK 1970-1990’ at Tate Britain, from which her work entered the Tate Collection, and through her shortlisting for the Max Mara Art Prize for Women. Her work is represented in major public collections including Tate, the British Museum, Cartwright Hall Art Gallery (Bradford), and Reading Museum & Art Gallery. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hunjan’s relationship with Bow Arts has been a long and collaborative one. Hunjan has worked as an artist-educator with Bow Arts since its inception and took part in one of the charity’s early Live Work spaces in 2007. She has developed numerous commissions for public artwork with Bow Arts and has held a studio in their P1 building since 2014.</p>

<header class="cta-headline"><h2 class="cta-heading"><a class=" has-red-color" href="https://bowarts.org/projects-stories/30-moments-for-30-years-artist-spotlight-bhajan-hunjan/">30 moments for 30 years Artist Spotlight: Bhajan Hunjan</a></h2></header>

<div class="cta-text"><p>As part of Bow Arts’ 30 for 30 reflection, Aoife Pallister Begadon spoke to artist Bhajan Hunjan, one of Bow Arts’ most established Artist Educators, about her journey alongside the arts charity from its inception.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access information</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Nunnery Gallery and Cafe have step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Accessible parking is not available on-site but blue badge parking can be found 500m away on Fairfield Road.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a table near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Opening hours: </strong>Wed-Sun, 10am to 4pm</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Address:</strong> Nunnery Gallery, 181 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Nearest station(s):</strong> Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bus:</strong> 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bike:</strong> Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>
